Subject: Capacity safety margin & queueing behavior for Dedicated pool

Hi Janelle,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited to move Acme onto Dedicated. Before we finalize the contract, Acme's infra team flagged a couple of runtime behaviors we want to make explicit in the SLA for the reserved GPU pool:

- A defined safety/headroom margin (they asked for a quantified floor so bursts don't immediately queue).
- Queueing/backpressure behavior when capacity is saturated (what we hold in queue, TTL, and failure modes).
- Failover to compatible model variants (and how that affects latency SLOs).

To keep procurement moving, would Acme accept an operational amendment that: 1) defines a 15-25% safety margin for baseline throughput (we can propose 20% as a starting point), 2) sets an explicit queue TTL (propose 45s) with documented fallback to a lower-cost model if durable headroom is exhausted, and 3) includes a 90-day credit if observed 95p latency exceeds the agreed thresholds more than twice in a month?

I've attached a short draft amendment (SLA_Amendment_Acme_v1.pdf) and a slice of our recent throughput logs to illustrate typical headroom. If that framing works, we can route a DocuSign amendment and lock the Dedicated pool after signatures.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will coordinate final pricing for the amendment, and Vivek can provide the technical appendix on queueing and eviction semantics.

Would appreciate a reply by EOD Wednesday so legal can prepare the change order.

Best,
Karthik

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A few clarifying questions from our infra/procurement side:

1) When you say \"safety/headroom margin,\" do you mean reserved extra capacity (i.e., physically idle GPUs) or a software-level admission buffer that prioritizes requests? Which of these do you guarantee if we pay for it?

2) Queue TTL: 45s seems reasonable but we need to understand the observable behavior if TTL expires — is the request dropped, retried, or routed to a fallback model? What error code will clients see?

3) Credits/SLAs: can you describe the measurement method for 95p latency? Which telemetry will we get access to for audit?

If you can answer those bullets and share the technical appendix Vivek mentioned, procurement will review and aim for an expedited amendment review. Also can you share a sample DocuSign flow?

Thanks,
Janelle Torres
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
janelle@acme.ai

Hi Janelle — quick answers below, Vivek included for technical confirmation:

1) Safety/headroom: this is an operational buffer expressed as a throughput floor per-customer within the reserved GPU pool. Practically, we do not keep GPUs permanently idle; instead the scheduler maintains a weighted admission buffer so that at normal traffic the customer sees ~20% additional admission capacity before new requests are queued. If you want physically idle GPUs reserved, we can price that as a dedicated headroom pool (higher cost) — note that committed idle capacity is billed differently.

2) Queue TTL: when TTL expires the request is failed with a 429 (or a 503 if downstream model fallback is unavailable). We offer two behaviors you can pick in the amendment: a) fail-fast 429, b) automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-latency/cheaper model with best-effort routing (this will change the response shape and latency). We'll describe the error codes in the appendix.

3) Measurement/telemetry: 95p latency is measured at the per-request gateway with token-level timestamps; we expose dashboards in the Redwood Console and send a daily SLO report. For audit we can provide a monthly CSV export of request-level metrics and a short sampling log for incidents.

I've attached the throughput logs slice we discussed; Vivek, can you confirm the proposed 45s TTL and whether 20% is realistic for steady bursts based on Acme's traffic profile?

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / Vivek —

I reviewed the ask and the traffic samples. My recommendation for Acme (to keep the procurement timeline short and minimize cost) is:

- Operational safety margin: commit to a 15% admission buffer by default, with an option for Acme to purchase a 10% physically reserved headroom bucket if they want guaranteed idle capacity (we'll add pricing line items).
- Queue TTL: agree to 45s for normal traffic, but specify that we will attempt automatic fallback to the compatible model for requests that hit the TTL; if fallback is used, latency SLOs for those requests are relaxed and won’t count as a breach for the premium model SLA (we will still measure and report them).
- Credits: 10% service credit for months where the measured 95p latency for premium model > SLA threshold more than twice.

I attached an SLA amendment stub that codifies the above. This structure keeps us flexible while giving Acme a clear operational outcome. If Acme prefers a higher safety margin we can upsell the reserved headroom bucket.

Next steps: Karthik, please send the amended doc to Janelle and include the DocuSign link. I'll lock pricing in HubSpot once we have a DocuSign intent. Vivek, please prepare the technical appendix that defines the error codes and the telemetry exports (short write-up).

-Marissa
